resources.string: Short brain games for a quick break, about a minute each. Offline, no ads, no subscription.
Echo: is the shape the same as the one before? Tap Yes or No, or swipe right for yes and left for no. The first card is just to remember. From level 10 you compare with the card two back.

Switches: lights roll out of the portal one after another. Tap a junction to flip it, so every light reaches the gate with its colour and shape. A round lasts 90 seconds, and the better you route, the closer the lights follow each other. 90% or more on target moves you up a level, below 70% down. Higher levels have more gates.

Constellation: a few stars light up in the night sky and go dark again. Tap where they were. Two wrong taps end the pass. A perfect pass draws the constellation and adds a star, one mistake keeps the count, two take one away.

Ink: does the meaning of the word on the left match the ink colour of the word on the right? Only the colour on the right counts, not what it says. Ink lives on colour and is only partly playable with strong colour blindness. Colour-blind mode keeps it to four colours that stay apart with red-green weakness.

Swarm: a swarm of comets shows up somewhere on the screen. Swipe the way the middle one with the ring points, whatever the others do. From level 10 the swarm also flies: if the middle one is hollow, swipe the way the swarm flies instead.

Bounce: glass prisms light up on the field for a moment and vanish. Then a light appears at the edge. Tap the edge where it will come out: every prism turns it by 90 degrees. A right answer moves you up a level, two wrong ones in a row move you down.

Drops: sums fall into the water. Type the answer on the keypad, the drop bursts. Drops with the same answer burst together, a golden drop clears the whole sky. Three drops in the water fill the basin and end the round, there is no clock. Solved drops make it faster, splashes slower.

Glance: keep your eyes on the cross in the middle. For a split second a shape flashes there and a star somewhere on the rings around it. Pick the shape with the two buttons and tap where the star was, in any order. Only both right counts. Two right answers make the flash shorter, a wrong one makes it longer. Short flashes depend on the screen: if a flash was shown noticeably too long or too short, the task does not count. On tablets and in landscape the field is bigger and feels different.

Slalom: your glider races through a crystal canyon at night. Tap the left or right half of the screen to switch lanes and dodge pillars and rocks, some of them slide sideways. Three hits end the round early. Every ten seconds without a hit it gets faster, a hit slows it down. A close dodge earns a bonus.
Every day thinkr picks up to three games for you. A game counts as soon as you have played a round of it today. One missed day per week does not break your streak.
Relaxed gives you half again as much time, with slower cards and lights, and keeps its own levels and best scores.
The games run against the clock and are hardly playable with a screen reader.
For fun. Not a medical device, no health claims.
